messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must drive at a safe speed for conditions. | Speed limits are posted in miles per hour (mph). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to comply can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians always have the right of way at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can result in traffic citations. | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading or unloading children.
• Stopping distance: 150 ft for 3‑axle buses, 200 ft for 4‑axle buses. | Violations can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Improper lane changes can result in a $50 fine. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | Violations may be ticketed or towed. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• “Stop” signs require a full stop even if the intersection is clear. | Running a red light can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense severity. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., TX‑130, TX‑130A).
• Toll rates vary by vehicle type and time of day. | Toll passes (e.g., TxTag) are available for frequent users. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial drivers must hold a valid CDL.
• Trucks over 26,000 lb must display a DOT number. | Violations can result in heavy fines and license revocation. | ### Quick Reference - **Seat belt**: $50 fine, 1 point. - **Hand‑held phone**: $50 fine, 1 point. - **DUI**: $500–$5,000 fine, 3–6 months license suspension, possible jail. - **School bus stop**: $200 fine. - **Red light**: $200 fine, 1 point. ### Resources - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code** – [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.HTM](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.HTM) - **Texas Highway Patrol** – [https://www.txdps.state.tx.us](https://www.txdps.state.tx.us) Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
